1	import React, { useState } from 'react';
2	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
3	import { useCustomerType, useShopperBasketsMutationHelper } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
4	import Seo from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo';
5	import { Box, Button, Center, Heading, Stack, Text } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
6	import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link';
7	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
8	import { API_ERROR_MESSAGE } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants';
9	// Zimmermann's own constant — NOT the base package above (see recommended-products/index.tsx's
10	// own comment on this exact gotcha: a named import off the base package's untyped module compiles
11	// but is undefined at runtime). APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX, not PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX — this page has no
12	// PageContainer/layerStyle second containment layer for PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX to correctly
13	// cancel; see that constant's own comment in app/constants/index.ts for the bug this distinction
14	// fixes (a real, live-confirmed horizontal overflow, Marcel, 2026-09-10).
15	import { APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX } from 'app/constants';
16	import { ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid } from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid';
17	import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
18	import { useRecentlyViewedHistory } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory';
19	import { useRecentlyViewedProductFetch } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch';
20	import {
21	  selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard,
22	  resolveOrderableVariant,
23	} from '../../utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard';
24	import type { RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard';
25	
26	// Message-id namespace follows this codebase's existing `<page>.<category>.<key>` convention
27	// (see home.*, product_list.*, product_detail.* in their own index.tsx files) -- `recently_viewed`
28	// is this page's own snake_case prefix.
29	const messages = defineMessages({
30	  title: {
31	    id: 'recently_viewed.heading.title',
32	    defaultMessage: 'Recently Viewed',
33	  },
34	  // Real ICU `plural` selector, not string interpolation -- decided explicitly this session
35	  // (build plan §B1, "go for it" -- Marcel, 2026-09-08). `#` is replaced by the matched `count`
36	  // value at each branch, so this renders "1 item" / "16 items" correctly with no separate
37	  // singular-check needed at the call site. Lowercase "item(s)" -- corrected 2026-09-11 (Marcel).
38	  itemCount: {
39	    id: 'recently_viewed.label.item_count',
40	    defaultMessage: '{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}',
41	  },
42	  emptyHeading: {
43	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.heading',
44	    defaultMessage: "You haven't viewed anything yet.",
45	  },
46	  emptyBodyRegistered: {
47	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.body_registered',
48	    defaultMessage: 'Continue shopping to start building your history.',
49	  },
50	  emptyBodyGuest: {
51	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.body_guest',
52	    defaultMessage: 'Sign in to keep track of your history, or continue shopping.',
53	  },
54	  continueShopping: {
55	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.cta.continue_shopping',
56	    defaultMessage: 'Continue Shopping',
57	  },
58	  signIn: {
59	    id: 'recently_viewed.empty.cta.sign_in',
60	    defaultMessage: 'Sign In',
61	  },
62	  // Same copy, same event, as product-list/index.tsx's own `product_list.toast.added_to_bag` --
63	  // a distinct message id under this page's own `recently_viewed.*` namespace (see this file's own
64	  // message-id-namespace comment above) rather than importing that page's message across a page
65	  // boundary.
66	  addedToBag: {
67	    id: 'recently_viewed.toast.added_to_bag',
68	    defaultMessage: 'Added to bag',
69	  },
70	});
71	
72	// Plain literal, not run through react-intl -- matches home/index.tsx's own un-translated Seo
73	// `description` precedent (`description="Commerce Cloud Retail React App"`). The build plan's
74	// SEO section only calls out `title` for useIntl; this page's own description copy was never
75	// specified, so it is authored here rather than invented as a translated message with no source.
76	const PAGE_DESCRIPTION = "Browse the products you've recently viewed at Zimmermann.";
77	
78	type EmptyRecentlyViewedProps = {
79	  isRegistered: boolean;
80	};
81	
82	/**
83	 * SFCC-84's own empty-state design (build plan §B2 "Empty state"). There is no AC or Figma design
84	 * for this state at all; copy and structure are ported from the real `EmptyCart` precedent
85	 * (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`), per
86	 * Marcel's own direction ("look for a pattern in the existing codebase and build off that"): a
87	 * `Box` > `Center` > `Stack` layout, an `isRegistered`-branched body message, and a
88	 * `Button as={Link}` CTA pattern (the base SFCC `Link`, not a raw `react-router-dom` one, so the
89	 * "Continue Shopping"/"Sign In" hrefs get this storefront's real multi-site URL prefixing --
90	 * `use-multi-site.js`'s `buildUrl`, called internally by that `Link` -- the same reason `EmptyCart`
91	 * itself uses it).
92	 *
93	 * **Deliberately not a byte-for-byte styling port.** `EmptyCart`'s own prop values
94	 * (`fontSize={['18px', '2xl']}`, `color="gray.700"`, `color="blue.600"`,
95	 * `width={['343px', '220px']}`) are raw base-Chakra literals with no relationship to Zimmermann's
96	 * design tokens, and this codebase's styling hierarchy
97	 * (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`) requires `textStyle`/`var(--zimm-*)` for new
98	 * Zimmermann-authored UI and forbids a raw px/rem literal outright. With no confirmed empty-state
99	 * Figma spec to derive exact values from, this uses the nearest reasonable *registered* tokens
100	 * (`heading2`/`body1` text styles, `text-default`/`text-secondary` colours, `2xl`/`2xs`/`m`
101	 * spacing) instead -- an autonomous styling judgement call (see this module's own bottom-of-file
102	 * decision log), not a design decision that conflicts with an existing one (there is no existing
103	 * design here to conflict with).
104	 *
105	 * **No icon.** `EmptyCart` renders `BasketIcon` above its heading and `AccountIcon` on its
106	 * "Sign In" button. Checked directly against `overrides/app/components/icons`' full export list:
107	 * no Recently-Viewed-thematic icon exists (no eye/clock/history glyph), and forcing an unrelated
108	 * one -- `BasketIcon` itself, or reusing `AccountIcon` -- would misrepresent this page rather than
109	 * help it, so both are omitted; heading + copy + CTA(s) alone still satisfies the established
110	 * empty-state pattern this page is following.
111	 *
112	 * `useIntl` is called directly in this leaf, not passed down as a prop -- this is the
113	 * Context-backed, app-wide exception `.claude/rules/components.md` > Composition documents for
114	 * `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` specifically (this is a private, single-parent sub-component of this page,
115	 * not a component exported from its own folder, so it needs no story/test of its own either --
116	 * its behaviour is exercised through this page's own `index.test.tsx`).
117	 */
118	const EmptyRecentlyViewed = ({ isRegistered }: EmptyRecentlyViewedProps) => {
119	  const intl = useIntl();
120	
121	  return (
122	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-empty">
123	      <Center>
124	        <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-2xl)" textAlign="center" paddingY="var(--zimm-scale-4xl)">
125	          <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-2xs)">
126	            <Text textStyle="heading2" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
127	              {intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyHeading)}
128	            </Text>
129	            <Text textStyle="body1" color="var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)">
130	              {isRegistered
131	                ? intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyBodyRegistered)
132	                : intl.formatMessage(messages.emptyBodyGuest)}
133	            </Text>
134	          </Stack>
135	          <Stack direction={{ base: 'column', sm: 'row' }} justify="center" spacing="var(--zimm-scale-m)">
136	            {/* Continue Shopping is the loud/primary CTA for a registered shopper (their only
137	                CTA), but yields primary emphasis to Sign In for a guest -- same isRegistered-driven
138	                emphasis flip EmptyCart's own solid/outline split encodes, re-expressed here via
139	                ZimmButton's own primary/secondary variants instead of a raw colour override. */}
140	            <Button
141	              as={Link}
142	              href="/"
143	              variant={isRegistered ? 'primary' : 'secondary'}
144	              width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }}
145	            >
146	              {intl.formatMessage(messages.continueShopping)}
147	            </Button>
148	            {!isRegistered && (
149	              <Button as={Link} href="/account" variant="primary" width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }}>
150	                {intl.formatMessage(messages.signIn)}
151	              </Button>
152	            )}
153	          </Stack>
154	        </Stack>
155	      </Center>
156	    </Box>
157	  );
158	};
159	
160	/**
161	 * SFCC-84 -- Recently Viewed Full History page container (build plan §B2). Thin container: reads
162	 * this shopper's tracked view history off `useRecentlyViewedHistory` (the same interim,
163	 * browser-tracked stand-in `RecommendedProducts`' own Recently-Viewed branch already uses -- see
164	 * that hook's own docblock for why Einstein is not the data source yet), fetches real product data
165	 * for those ids via `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch` (capped at 24 internally already -- nothing
166	 * further to cap here), maps each result through `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` (filtering
167	 * the hard `null` gate every mapper in this codebase uses), and renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` --
168	 * or, with no tracked history, this page's own empty state (`EmptyRecentlyViewed` above).
169	 *
170	 * **Known, already-flagged gap, not introduced here:** `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`'s
171	 * `badge` field is always `undefined` -- the plain `getProducts` endpoint this build reads from has
172	 * no confirmed `c_productBadges` field (see that mapper's own docblock's "Badge" section). A card
173	 * rendered by this page will never show a badge yet; this is a pre-existing, out-of-scope gap for
174	 * this step, not a bug in this file.
175	 *
176	 * **Empty-state gate: `hasRecentlyViewed` (`recentlyViewedIds.length > 0`), not
177	 * `cards.length === 0`.** The two are equivalent for a shopper who has never viewed anything, but
178	 * diverge while `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch`'s own request is still in flight for a shopper who
179	 * *does* have tracked ids: `cards` is `[]` until that fetch resolves (see that hook's own
180	 * `isLoading` field, unused here for the same reason `RecommendedProducts`' own Recently-Viewed
181	 * branch doesn't reference it either -- no loading skeleton exists for this fetch anywhere in this
182	 * build yet). Gating on `cards.length === 0` would flash this page's own empty-state copy for a
183	 * real returning shopper before the grid ever gets a chance to render. Gating on
184	 * `hasRecentlyViewed` instead avoids that race entirely -- a shopper with real tracked ids never
185	 * sees "you haven't viewed anything," even momentarily. The one residual case the two signals can
186	 * still disagree on -- every tracked id failing to hydrate into a usable card (e.g. every product
187	 * deleted/offline since it was viewed) -- is a real, accepted edge case, not solved here:
188	 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` itself renders `null` for an empty `cards` array by its own documented
189	 * contract, so that narrow case renders blank content rather than either this page's populated
190	 * grid or its own empty-state copy. Reusing the history hook's own `hasRecentlyViewed` (rather
191	 * than re-deriving `recentlyViewedIds.length === 0` locally) also keeps this page's gate
192	 * automatically in sync with that hook's own definition of "has history" -- the same value
193	 * `RecommendedProducts`' own AC-8 gate already uses for the rail.
194	 *
195	 * **SSR note, inherited from the hook, not new here:** `useRecentlyViewedHistory` starts every
196	 * render (including the server-rendered one) at `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`
197	 * and only resolves real browser storage inside a `useEffect` -- so the very first paint of this
198	 * page, even for a real returning shopper's browser, renders this page's own empty state until
199	 * hydration completes. This is an existing, accepted property of that hook (already true for the
200	 * rail this page complements), not something this container introduces or attempts to fix.
201	 *
202	 * **SEO -- `noindex, nofollow`, via `Seo`'s `children`, not its `noIndex` prop.** Base `Seo`
203	 * (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/index.jsx:20`) emits
204	 * `<meta name="robots" content="noindex" />` for `noIndex` -- `noindex` only, never `nofollow`.
205	 * Passing both `noIndex` and an explicit `<meta name="robots">` child would emit two competing
206	 * `robots` tags, so `noIndex` is left unset and the full directive is passed as a child instead
207	 * (Marcel's explicit decision, build plan §B2). `<Seo>` is otherwise mounted exactly as
208	 * `home/index.tsx` mounts it -- `title`/`description` only, no extra props.
209	 *
210	 * `getTemplateName` matches the convention already used by every other page-level override
211	 * (`home`, `product-detail`, `product-list`, `experience`, `contentful-preview` -- see each file's
212	 * own `<Page>.getTemplateName = () => '<name>';` line, placed the same way here).
213	 */
214	const RecentlyViewed = () => {
215	  const intl = useIntl();
216	  const { isRegistered } = useCustomerType();
217	  const { hasRecentlyViewed, recentlyViewedIds } = useRecentlyViewedHistory();
218	  const { products } = useRecentlyViewedProductFetch(recentlyViewedIds);
219	  const toast = useToast();
220	  const { addItemToNewOrExistingBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutationHelper();
221	
222	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's and recommended-products/index.tsx's own
223	  // consumers already use: formatPrice is injected into the mapper rather than formatted inside
224	  // it, keeping that mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
225	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string): string =>
226	    intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
227	
228	  // Size-aware Add to Bag (2026-09-09 full-parity-with-PLP build) -- keyed by product id rather
229	  // than product-list/index.tsx's own per-card `ProductListCard` wrapper with local `useState`:
230	  // that pattern needs a per-card component instance to own its own state, but this page's grid
231	  // (`ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`) is a shared, already-shipped organism that renders `cards` directly
232	  // with no per-card wrapper slot of its own (unlike PLP, which builds its own grid inline with
233	  // full control) -- touching that organism's contract to add one would be a bigger, cross-cutting
234	  // change than this fix calls for (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5: never refactor upward). A single
235	  // id-keyed map at this container achieves the same "each card remembers its own selected size"
236	  // result without touching the Grid at all.
237	  const [selectedSizeChipValues, setSelectedSizeChipValues] = useState<Record<string, string | undefined>>({});
238	
239	  const handleResolvedAddToBag = (orderableProductId: string, price: number | undefined) => {
240	    addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([{ productId: orderableProductId, price, quantity: 1 }])
241	      .then(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToBag), status: 'success' }))
242	      .catch(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE), status: 'error' }));
243	  };
244	
245	  const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = products
246	    .map((product): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
247	      const card = selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard(product, formatPrice);
248	      if (!card) return null;
249	
250	      const selectedSizeChipValue = selectedSizeChipValues[product.id];
251	      return {
252	        ...card,
253	        selectedSizeChipValue,
254	        onSizeChipSelect: (value: string) =>
255	          setSelectedSizeChipValues((previous) => ({ ...previous, [product.id]: value })),
256	        onAddToBag: () => {
257	          // No selection -> default-variant behaviour (matches product-list/index.tsx's own
258	          // ProductListCard.handleAddToBag exactly): no size selected means default size. A
259	          // selection that somehow matches no real variant falls back the same way, rather than
260	          // blocking the add entirely on a data mismatch.
261	          const resolved = selectedSizeChipValue ? resolveOrderableVariant(product, selectedSizeChipValue) : null;
262	          handleResolvedAddToBag(resolved?.productId ?? product.id, resolved?.price ?? product.price);
263	        },
264	      };
265	    })
266	    .filter((card): card is RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard => card !== null);
267	
268	  const title = intl.formatMessage(messages.title);
269	
270	  return (
271	    <Box data-testid="recently-viewed-page">
272	      <Seo title={title} description={PAGE_DESCRIPTION}>
273	        <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow" />
274	      </Seo>
275	      {/* Screen-reader-only page heading — 2026-09-10, closing a real gap: this page had no
276	       * Heading element at all in either branch below, breaking the pattern product-list/index.tsx
277	       * and product-detail/index.tsx both already follow, and leaving up to
278	       * RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED real <h3> product-name headings (ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid)
279	       * with nothing above them in the heading hierarchy (WCAG 2.2 AA 1.3.1/2.4.6). `srOnly`,
280	       * matching product-detail/index.tsx's own <h1> exactly — the page's own visible title
281	       * styling (ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid's own textStyle="heading3" span, unchanged here) is a
282	       * separate, wider pre-existing pattern (several other organisms do the same thing) and out
283	       * of scope for this fix. */}
284	      <Heading as="h1" srOnly>
285	        {title}
286	      </Heading>
287	      {hasRecentlyViewed ? (
288	        // Bleeds the grid edge-to-edge past #app-main's own sitewide padding, matching the
289	        // Recently Viewed Rail's own flush treatment (product-detail/product-list's
290	        // <RecommendedProducts mx={PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX}>) — confirmed against this page's own
291	        // three real Figma frames (9551:78221 Desktop / 9560:137688 Tablet / 9560:138459 Mobile,
292	        // Zimmermann_Designs file), which show the header and every Product Card Group spanning
293	        // the full frame width, not inset within a page margin. ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid itself has
294	        // no passthrough/mx slot (unlike RecommendedProducts, which forwards `{...props}` to its
295	        // own wrapping Box for exactly this reason), so the bleed is applied here at the page
296	        // level instead. EmptyRecentlyViewed below is a distinct, centred layout with no

211	 * A component for fetching and rendering product recommendations from the Einstein API

217	  products,
218	  title,

220	  ...props
221	}: RecommendedProductsProps) => {
222	  const { isLoading, recommendations, getZoneRecommendations, getRecommendations, sendClickReco, sendViewReco } =

225	  const { customerId } = customer;
226	  const { data: wishlist } = useWishList();

229	  const createCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('createCustomerProductListItem');
230	  const deleteCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('deleteCustomerProductListItem');
231	  const toast = useToast();
232	  const navigate = useNavigation();
233	  const intl = useIntl();
234	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's own consumer uses

236	  // mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.

238	
239	  const ref = useRef();
240	  const isOnScreen = useIntersectionObserver(ref, { useOnce: true });
241	  const [_products, setProducts] = useState(products);
242	  // Cart-exclusion check (2026-09-10, Marcel: "no recently viewed on cart" — a standing product

247	  // node_modules/.../constants.js:154-160), so the recommender check below cannot tell the two

323	    // Cart exclusion (2026-09-10, Marcel) — see the isCartPage constant's own comment above for
324	    // why this can't be expressed as a distinct recommender value. No rail, no title, no

326	    if (isCartPage) {

383	          cards={cards}

389	  }

391	  // The component should remove itself altogether if it has no recommendations
392	  // and we aren't loading any.
393	  if (!isLoading && (!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1)) {
394	    return null;
395	  }
396	
397	  // TODO: DRY this handler when intl provider is available globally
398	  const addItemToWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
399	    try {
400	      if (!wishlist || !customerId) {
401	        return;
402	      }
403	      await createCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
404	        parameters: {
405	          listId: wishlist.id,
406	          customerId,
407	        },
408	        body: {
409	          quantity: 1,
410	          productId: product.productId,
411	          public: false,
412	          priority: 1,
413	          type: 'product',
414	        },
415	      });
416	
417	      toast({
418	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST, { quantity: 1 }),

420	        action: (
421	          // it would be better if we could use <Button as={Link}>
422	          // but unfortunately the Link component is not compatible
423	          // with Chakra Toast, since the ToastManager is rendered via portal
424	          // and the toast doesn't have access to intl provider, which is a
425	          // requirement of the Link component.
426	          <Button variant="link" onClick={() => navigate('/account/wishlist')}>
427	            {intl.formatMessage(TOAST_ACTION_VIEW_WISHLIST)}
428	          </Button>
429	        ),
430	      });
431	    } catch {
432	      toast({
433	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
434	        status: 'error',
435	      });
436	    }
437	  };
438

441	      const wishlistItem = wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.find(

455	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_REMOVED_FROM_WISHLIST),
456	        status: 'success',
457	        id: product.productId,

459	    } catch {
460	      toast({
461	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
462	        status: 'error',
463	      });

465	  };

467	  return (
468	    <ProductScroller
469	      ref={ref}
470	      title={title || recommendations?.displayMessage}
471	      products={recommendations.recs}
472	      isLoading={isLoading}
473	      productTileProps={(product: RecommendedProduct) => ({
474	        onClick: () => {
475	          sendClickReco(
476	            {
477	              recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
478	              __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,

1	/**
2	 * Maps one Recently Viewed product to the FULL `ZimmProductCard` props Recently Viewed's Full
3	 * History page (SFCC-84) renders — badge, size chips, was/now pricing and a multi-image gallery,
4	 * i.e. the `plp` variation's already-shipped shape, not `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s narrower
5	 * image-only rail shape (SFCC-83's `recentlyViewed` variation). Both mappers read the same
6	 * underlying input — a plain Commerce API `Product` from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
7	 * `getProducts` call — but produce deliberately different output shapes for two deliberately
8	 * different surfaces; see that mapper's own docblock for the rail's narrower contract and why it
9	 * stops at image-only.
10	 *
11	 * Added per the build plan's B2 discussion (finding 41b): "reuse the rail's mapper" was the
12	 * original, incorrect assumption for this page — `recentlyViewedCard.ts` cannot produce this
13	 * shape by its own design (image-only, no price, no gallery), so a second, separate mapper is
14	 * required. Per Jasmijn's SFCC-84 comment, the Full History card's default state is "image, name,
15	 * badge, price (incl. was/now), and cart icon" — exactly the `plp` variation's shape, which is why
16	 * this mapper's output includes `headingLevel: 'h3'` and `variation: 'plp'` directly (unlike
17	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s `RecentlyViewedCard`, which deliberately excludes both as its rail
18	 * container's job) — mirroring `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult`, which
19	 * bakes in the same two fields for the same reason: its output is meant to be spread straight
20	 * into `<ZimmProductCard>` with nothing left for a caller to add.
21	 *
22	 * Modelled on `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s general style/docblock conventions (no React/react-intl
23	 * import, `formatPrice` injected as a parameter, same hard `null`-gate contract for a product
24	 * with no usable name/image) and on `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`
25	 * (the closest existing precedent producing this exact `plp`-variation output shape from a real
26	 * product). Ported, not imported, from both — a genuinely separate, self-contained module with
27	 * its own local type aliases, the same relationship `recentlyViewedCard.ts` already has to
28	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` (see that file's own docblock).
29	 *
30	 * **What's ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`, and what changed:**
31	 * `selectSizeChipValues` is re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly (the plain
32	 * `Product` shape) in place of a `ProductSearchHit`'s own same-named field — the underlying
33	 * `VariationAttribute` shape is the same `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` type either way, so the
34	 * picking/mapping logic itself needed no change, only the input type.
35	 *
36	 * **Image resolution — revised 2026-09-09 to close the same real bug already fixed on
37	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedCard.ts`: a colour-blind image pick, and API array
38	 * order trusted over the image filename's own sequence number.** `selectGalleryImages` used to
39	 * pick "whichever image group has the most images," viewtype-agnostic — actually a worse version
40	 * of the same bug: no colour scoping meant a multi-colour product's gallery could mix different
41	 * colours' photos, and no viewtype restriction meant it could pick a non-`medium` group (an
42	 * oversized image at thumbnail size, against AGENTS.md's image-sizing rule). Now shares one
43	 * `selectColourScopedImages` resolution — colour-scoped `filterImageGroups` first (colour from
44	 * `resolveViewedColour`, which is only ever the fallback half of `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
45	 * `resolveRepresentativeColour`: this input has no `representedProduct` field, see that function's
46	 * own doc), falling back to a viewtype-only match for a genuinely single-colour product whose one
47	 * group carries no colour tag at all, then sorted by the image filename's own sequence number
48	 * (same real defect: a colour-tagged group can come back `[2, 1, ...]`, not ascending). This one
49	 * array now feeds `primaryImage`, `primaryImageFallbacks`, `hoverImage` and `images` — mirroring
50	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectProductListCard` exactly, except `primaryImage` is the
51	 * array's own first entry rather than a separately-sourced `hit.image` (a plain `getProducts`
52	 * `Product` has no equivalent flat `image` field — a Search-hit-only convenience field) — the same
53	 * adaptation `recentlyViewedCard.ts` already made for its own single-image case.
54	 *
55	 * **Price handling is deliberately NOT copied from `productListCardMapper.ts`.** That mapper reads
56	 * the flat `hit.price` field for `currentPrice` while leaving `originalPrice` unset entirely — had
57	 * it called `getPriceData(hit).listPrice` for `originalPrice` while keeping `hit.price` for
58	 * `currentPrice`, the two would risk disagreeing on a multi-variant product, since `getPriceData`

62	 * confirmed by reading it directly) so the two halves can never disagree. `originalPrice` is only

68	 * unconfirmed whether the `getProducts` hydration endpoint populates this custom attribute at all

72	 * `useProduct` call): the field is genuinely present — `c_productBadges: [{productBadge: 'Runway',

75	 * product. Interestingly, the *same* product's Search hit carried no `c_productBadges` at all at
76	 * the same moment — most likely the search index simply hadn't caught up yet with a recently-added

79	 * hypothesis, not independently re-verified here.
80	 *
81	 * `productBadgeUrl` is a real field on the live data above, discovered by this check — not
82	 * consumed here or anywhere in this codebase today. `badge` stays a plain label string (matching
83	 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps.badge?: string`, and `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own read of the same
84	 * shape) — turning a badge into a link is a real, undesigned UI decision, not something to invent
85	 * silently here.

139	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
140	
141	/** The variation-attribute id this mapper reads for size chips — named per conventions.md's
142	 *  no-magic-strings rule. `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectSizeChipValues`, which this is
143	 *  ported from, uses the literal inline; named here instead since this is a fresh file. */
144	const SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'size';
145	
146	/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
147	 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */
148	const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
149	
150	/**
151	 * Resolves which real colour this product's images should come from — now the shared
152	 * `resolveFallbackColour` (`productCardMappingHelpers.ts`) directly, same as
153	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s identical `resolveViewedColour`: there is no `representedProduct`
154	 * branch to add here, since this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` (from
155	 * `getProducts`), which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type).
156	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` layers exactly one extra branch
157	 * (a `representedProduct` match, Search-hit-only) in front of this same shared fallback. Returns
158	 * `undefined` when there are no variants at all — `selectColourScopedImages` below then falls back
159	 * to an unscoped, viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
160	 */
161	const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): string | undefined =>
162	  resolveFallbackColour(product.variants, COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
163	
164	/**
165	 * Sorts by the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into each image's own filename
166	 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`) — confirmed live on `4673TS251`,
167	 * whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`.
168	 *
169	 * Shared with `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedCard.ts` — see
170	 * `productCardMappingHelpers.ts`'s own docblock for why a shared primitive rather than three
171	 * separate copies (all three had drifted onto the identical non-transitive-comparator bug,
172	 * CodeRabbit 2026-09-10).
173	 */
174	const sortByImageSequence = (images: ZimmProductCardImage[]): ZimmProductCardImage[] =>
175	  sortImagesBySequence(images, (image) => image.src);
176	
177	/**
178	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`, confirmed by reading
179	 * it directly), narrowed to the three fields this mapper reads. `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
180	 * ships no TypeScript types — this subpath falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s
181	 * catch-all `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'`, a shorthand ambient module
182	 * declaration that types the whole module `any`, so `getPriceData`'s real return is implicitly
183	 * `any`. Declaring a local, narrow type for the fields actually read — rather than letting that
184	 * `any` propagate into this module's own types — matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
185	 * narrow-local-type pattern for the same untyped function (typescript.md's no-`any` rule). This
186	 * is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee: TypeScript allows
187	 * assigning `any` to any narrower type with no check, so the real correctness proof is the test
188	 * file's own direct comparison against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
189	 */
190	type SfccPriceData = {
191	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — never `product.price` directly. This is the field
192	   *  `productListCardMapper.ts` does not use for its own `currentPrice` (it reads the flat
193	   *  `hit.price` field instead) — see this module's own docblock for why that risks disagreeing
194	   *  with a `getPriceData`-derived `originalPrice` on a multi-variant product. */
195	  currentPrice: number;
196	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the product has no
197	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
198	  listPrice: number | undefined;
199	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`
200	   *  (a numeric comparison against `undefined` evaluates to `false` in JS, never throws). */
201	  isOnSale: boolean;
202	};
203	
204	/** The real `imageGroups[].images[]` element shape (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own
205	 *  `ShopperProductsTypes.Image`) — named `RawImage` to match `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
206	 *  local name for the equivalent concept, but pointed at the real SDK type rather than that
207	 *  file's hand-rolled shape (AGENTS.md > Type Definitions: don't re-declare a type the SDK
208	 *  already exports). */
209	type RawImage = ShopperProductsTypes.Image;
210	
211	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
212	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
213	  if (!src) return undefined;
214	  return { src, alt: toGalleryAlt(image?.alt) };
215	};
216	
217	/**
218	 * The colour + `medium`-viewtype-scoped image list this product's card uses — one lookup feeding
219	 * four separate things below (`primaryImage`, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the
220	 * broken-image fallback candidates), so none of them can ever disagree with each other or with the
221	 * resolved colour. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
222	 * `selectColourScopedImages`, re-pointed at `product.imageGroups` (the plain `getProducts` shape)
223	 * in place of a `ProductSearchHit`'s own same-named field — the underlying `ImageGroup`/`Image`
224	 * types are identical either way (confirmed directly against
225	 * `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`).
226	 *
227	 * **Two-pass, not one** — same real bug as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own version closes: a
228	 * strict colour-scoped `filterImageGroups` match requires the group to explicitly declare a
229	 * matching `variationAttributes` entry, but a single-colour product's medium group commonly
230	 * carries no `variationAttributes` at all (nothing to disambiguate), which would make a
231	 * colour-scoped-only lookup exclude the group and return nothing. Falls back to a viewtype-only
232	 * match in that case. Never the reverse — a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
233	 * avoid re-mixing colours.
234	 */
235	const selectColourScopedImages = (
236	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
237	  colour: string | undefined,
238	): ZimmProductCardImage[] => {
239	  const colourScopedGroups = colour
240	    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
241	        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
242	        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
243	      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
244	    : [];
245	
246	  const groups =
247	    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
248	      ? colourScopedGroups
249	      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
250	          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
251	        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);
252	
253	  const images = (groups[0]?.images ?? [])
254	    .map(toCardImage)
255	    .filter((image): image is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(image));
256	
257	  return sortByImageSequence(images);
258	};
259	
260	/**
261	 * Picks this product's gallery from the colour-scoped image list above — matches
262	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for 0 or 1 images (returns `undefined`, never
263	 * a 1-length array). Kept exported and independently tested, same as
264	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` — `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`
265	 * below calls `selectColourScopedImages` directly instead (one shared computation feeding
266	 * `primaryImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks`/`hoverImage`/`images` at once), matching that file's own
267	 * documented, deliberate minor redundancy rather than introducing a new one.
268	 */
269	export const selectGalleryImages = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
270	  const images = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
271	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
272	};
273	
274	/**
275	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this product has one) into the shape
276	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
277	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly — `orderable` on
278	 * each value already reflects real stock for that specific size, so it maps directly to
279	 * `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
280	 */
281	export const selectSizeChipValues = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
282	  const sizeAttribute = product.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
283	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
284	    value: value.value,
285	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
286	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
287	  }));
288	};
289	
290	/** What `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves a selected size chip value to — same shape, same
291	 *  reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ResolvedVariant`: the real, orderable SKU for
292	 *  that specific size, not the master id this product otherwise defaults to. */
293	export type ResolvedVariant = {
294	  productId: string;
295	  price: number | undefined;
296	  orderable: boolean;
297	};
298	
299	/**
300	 * Resolves a selected size CHIP VALUE to its real orderable variant — ported near-verbatim from
301	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveOrderableVariant`, re-pointed at this input's own
302	 * `variants` field (identical shape either way — both are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` `Variant`
303	 * types). Returns `null` when there is no matching variant at all — callers fall back to this
304	 * product's own default id/price in that case, the same default that already existed before
305	 * size-aware Add to Bag was ever selectable.
306	 */
307	export const resolveOrderableVariant = (
308	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
309	  sizeValue: string,
310	): ResolvedVariant | null => {
311	  const variant = product.variants?.find((candidate) => candidate.variationValues?.size === sizeValue);
312	  if (!variant) return null;
313	
314	  return {
315	    productId: variant.productId,
316	    price: variant.price,
317	    orderable: variant.orderable !== false,
318	  };
319	};
320	
321	/**
322	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(product)` call — see this
323	 * module's own docblock for why both must come from the same call rather than mixing a flat
324	 * `product.price` field for one and `getPriceData` for the other. No `opts` passed — the default
325	 * `quantity: 1` is correct for a single-unit card display (matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
326	 * no-opts calls for the same reason). No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
327	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed, matching `productInfo.ts`'s and
328	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" rule.
329	 */
330	const selectPriceFields = (
331	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
332	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
333	): Pick<RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
334	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(product);
335	
336	  const currentPrice =
337	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && product.currency
338	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, product.currency)
339	      : undefined;
340	
341	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale product must not render a crossed-out price
342	  // identical to its current one.
343	  const originalPrice =
344	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && product.currency
345	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, product.currency)
346	      : undefined;
347	
348	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
349	};
350	
351	/**
352	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
353	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
354	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
355	 * @returns Props for the `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard`, or `null` when the product has no
356	 *   usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw. Same hard-gate contract
357	 *   as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard`. `onAddToBag`/`selectedSizeChipValue`/
358	 *   `onSizeChipSelect` are deliberately not populated here — same split
359	 *   `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` documents: this mapper is a pure data
360	 *   function with no per-card selection state of its own, so the page container wires those three
361	 *   (see `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own per-card size-chip state).
362	 */
363	export const selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = (
364	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct | undefined | null,
365	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
366	): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
367	  if (!product?.name) return null;
368	
369	  // One resolution feeds primaryImage, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the broken-image
370	  // fallback candidates below — see selectColourScopedImages's own docblock for why.
371	  const scopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
372	  const [firstImage] = scopedImages;
373	  if (!firstImage) return null;
374	
375	  // Required-non-empty alt for the primary position only — shared resolveRequiredAlt
376	  // (productCardMappingHelpers.ts, also used by recentlyViewedCard.ts's own primary image). Was
377	  // `firstImage.alt || product.name` here (no `.trim()`) until 2026-09-10, a real gap this shared
378	  // helper closes: a whitespace-only alt is a non-empty string, so it passed straight through
379	  // instead of falling back — confirmed with a real whitespace-only-alt repro. The rest of
380	  // scopedImages keeps toCardImage's plain alt (matching productListCardMapper.ts's own gallery
381	  // images, which get no such treatment either) since only the primary slot ever carried this
382	  // extra safeguard.
383	  const primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage = { ...firstImage, alt: resolveRequiredAlt(firstImage.alt, product.name) };
384	
385	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(product, formatPrice);
386	
387	  return {
388	    id: product.id,
389	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
390	    name: product.name,
391	    headingLevel: 'h3',
392	    primaryImage,
393	    // Ordered backup candidates if primaryImage itself fails to load — same real, live defect
394	    // productListCardMapper.ts's own primaryImageFallbacks closes.
395	    primaryImageFallbacks: scopedImages,
396	    // The second image in the same colour-scoped sequence — revealed on hover. undefined when
397	    // there is no second image, which ZimmProductCardMedia already treats as "no swap".
398	    hoverImage: scopedImages[1],
399	    images: scopedImages.length > 1 ? scopedImages : undefined,
400	    currentPrice,
401	    originalPrice,
402	    // product.master is this master product's own overall orderability (ShopperProductsTypes.Master
403	    // — confirmed via the SDK's own type) — the equivalent of productListCardMapper.ts's flat
404	    // hit.orderable for this input shape, which has no such flat field of its own.
405	    isUnavailable: product.master?.orderable === false,
406	    // Single highest-priority badge -- confirmed live, 2026-09-09 (see this module's own docblock's
407	    // "Badge" section). SFCC-225's own hook already sorts c_productBadges by badgePriorityOrder
408	    // before this ever reaches the frontend, matching productListCardMapper.ts's own identical read.
409	    badge: product.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,
410	    variation: 'plp',
411	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(product),
412	  };
413	};

1	/**
2	 * The "given IDs, fetch real product data" half of SFCC-83/84's interim Recently Viewed data
3	 * source (build plan §2, "Interim data source" — Einstein is "Not Deployed" on every real
4	 * Zimmermann site, so this build ships against a browser-tracked view-history stand-in instead).
5	 * The companion piece is `useRecentlyViewedHistory`
6	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`), which supplies the `ids` this hook
7	 * consumes — every product this hook returns is real, live Commerce Cloud data; only the list of
8	 * *which* IDs to fetch is sourced from this browser's own tracked history rather than Einstein.
9	 *
10	 * Wraps `useProducts` (`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, confirmed real export at
11	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.js`, re-exported from
12	 * the package root — the same hook already used at
13	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:334`), which calls the Shopper Products
14	 * `getProducts` endpoint. Parameters (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [
15	 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`) match the combination already confirmed
16	 * correct three independent times this build (Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails`
17	 * — `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505` — the PLP quick-test mapper,
18	 * and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's real-product search call).
19	 *
20	 * **The 24-ID cap is a real, hard API limit, not a preference.** Confirmed directly in the SDK's
21	 * own doc comment: `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.js:29`
22	 * — *"The maximum number of productIDs that can be requested are 24."* — restated independently
23	 * in `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own type-declaration prose
24	 * (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:58802`: *"hydrate a list of products
25	 * (max 24)"*). Marcel's explicit decision: cap to the first `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST`
26	 * ids, don't batch into multiple requests — a shopper with more than 24 tracked IDs simply never
27	 * gets the tail of their history fetched by this hook.
28	 *
29	 * **SDK param widening for `ids`.** `getProductsQueryParameters.ids` types as `Array<string>`
30	 * throughout `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` (confirmed at `index.esm.d.ts:57797` and `:58753`), but the
31	 * real, working base SFCC call this build models (`use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails`)
32	 * passes a comma-joined string (`ids.join(',')`) straight through — the SDK forwards it verbatim
33	 * into the query string regardless of the declared array type. This file follows the exact same
34	 * precedent already used elsewhere in this codebase for this exact field:
35	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:339`
36	 * (`ids: childVariantIds.join(',') as unknown as string[]`, commented there as "SDK param
37	 * widening").
38	 */
39	import { useProducts } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
40	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
41	import { RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED } from 'app/constants';
42	
43	/**
44	 * Hard per-request limit on the Shopper Products `getProducts` endpoint — see this file's own
45	 * docblock above for the two independent SDK citations confirming this number. Not a UX/product
46	 * choice, and not adjustable client-side.
47	 *
48	 * Same fact as `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (`app/constants`) — that constant's own
49	 * storage cap was deliberately lowered to match this fetch limit once it was discovered (see its
50	 * own comment), not chosen independently, so this aliases the same value rather than retyping it.
51	 */
52	const GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST = RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED;
53	
54	export type RecentlyViewedProductFetchResult = {
55	  /**
56	   * Real Shopper Products data for as many of the requested (capped) `ids` as the API actually
57	   * returned, **re-ordered to match `ids`'s own order** — the API's own response order is not
58	   * documented or guaranteed to match request order, so this hook does the re-ordering rather
59	   * than assume it. An id the API didn't return at all (e.g. offline or deleted since it was
60	   * viewed) is silently dropped, not left as a hole in the array.
61	   */
62	  products: readonly ShopperProductsTypes.Product[];
63	  /** `true` only while a real fetch is in flight for a non-empty id list — deliberately `false`,
64	   *  not the underlying query's own (potentially permanently-pending) loading state, when there
65	   *  are no ids to fetch at all, since no request is ever made in that case. */
66	  isLoading: boolean;
67	};
68	
69	/**
70	 * Given a list of product IDs (most-recent-first, per `useRecentlyViewedHistory`), fetches real,
71	 * live Commerce Cloud product data for them.
72	 *
73	 * @param ids - Product IDs to fetch, most-recent-first. A list longer than
74	 *   `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST` is truncated to the first N (Marcel's cap-don't-batch
75	 *   decision) — the endpoint itself has no way to serve more in a single call.
76	 * @returns `products` — real product data for the requested ids, re-ordered to match `ids` and
77	 *   with any id the API didn't return dropped. `isLoading` — whether a real fetch is in flight.
78	 */
79	export const useRecentlyViewedProductFetch = (ids: readonly string[]): RecentlyViewedProductFetchResult => {
80	  const cappedIds = ids.slice(0, GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST);
81	
82	  const { data, isLoading: queryIsLoading } = useProducts(
83	    {
84	      parameters: {
85	        // SDK param widening -- see this file's own docblock for why a comma-joined string is
86	        // correct here despite the declared `Array<string>` type.
87	        ids: cappedIds.join(',') as unknown as string[],
88	        allImages: true,
89	        perPricebook: true,
90	        expand: ['prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations'],
91	      },
92	    },
93	    {
94	      // Matches the existing precedent at product-detail/index.tsx:347 for this same hook: don't
95	      // fire a request at all when there's nothing to ask for.
96	      enabled: cappedIds.length > 0,
97	    },
98	  );
99	
100	  const productsById = new Map((data?.data ?? []).map((product) => [product.id, product] as const));
101	  const products = cappedIds
102	    .map((id) => productsById.get(id))
103	    .filter((product): product is ShopperProductsTypes.Product => product !== undefined);
104	
105	  return {
106	    products,
107	    // A disabled query (no ids) never transitions out of its initial loading state on some
108	    // TanStack Query versions/configurations -- AND against `cappedIds.length > 0` so "loading"
109	    // never lies about a fetch that was never actually started.
110	    isLoading: cappedIds.length > 0 && queryIsLoading,
111	  };
112	};

input.old_string:
* **Empty-state gate: `hasRecentlyViewed` (`recentlyViewedIds.length > 0`), not
 * `cards.length === 0`.** The two are equivalent for a shopper who has never viewed anything, but
 * diverge while `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch`'s own request is still in flight for a shopper who
 * *does* have tracked ids: `cards` is `[]` until that fetch resolves (see that hook's own
 * `isLoading` field, unused here for the same reason `RecommendedProducts`' own Recently-Viewed
 * branch doesn't reference it either -- no loading skeleton exists for this fetch anywhere in this
 * build yet). Gating on `cards.length === 0` would flash this page's own empty-state copy for a
 * real returning shopper before the grid ever gets a chance to render. Gating on
 * `hasRecentlyViewed` instead avoids that race entirely -- a shopper with real tracked ids never
 * sees "you haven't viewed anything," even momentarily. The one residual case the two signals can
 * still disagree on -- every tracked id failing to hydrate into a usable card (e.g. every product
 * deleted/offline since it was viewed) -- is a real, accepted edge case, not solved here:
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` itself renders `null` for an empty `cards` array by its own documented
 * contract, so that narrow case renders blank content rather than either this page's populated
 * grid or its own empty-state copy. Reusing the history hook's own `hasRecentlyViewed` (rather
 * than re-deriving `recentlyViewedIds.length === 0` locally) also keeps this page's gate
 * automatically in sync with that hook's own definition of "has history" -- the same value
 * `RecommendedProducts`' own AC-8 gate already uses for the rail.
 *
 * **SSR note, inherited from the hook, not new here:** `useRecentlyViewedHistory` starts every
 * render (including the server-rendered one) at `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`
 * and only resolves real browser storage inside a `useEffect` -- so the very first paint of this
 * page, even for a real returning shopper's browser, renders this page's own empty state until
 * hydration completes. This is an existing, accepted property of that hook (already true for the
 * rail this page complements), not something this container introduces or attempts to fix.
 *

 * `isLoading` still `true`, request in flight, no recs yet) renders neither -- the same principle

content.text:
## Branch check

`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein` — not `develop`/`main`. Confirmed before touching anything.

## What changed, and why it matters

**Consequence:** Before this step, the Full History page (`/recently-viewed`) still ran on the interim browser-storage mechanism E1 already retired from the Rail. Left as-is, E4 (deleting those two interim files) would have broken this page's build outright. Now it doesn't — the page reads real Einstein data the same way the Rail already does, and a returning shopper's Add-to-Bag/size-selection still resolves the same variant it did before.

**Mechanism:** `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` called `useRecentlyViewedHistory()` + `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch()` to get a shopper's tracked IDs and hydrate them. I replaced that with `useEinstein()` directly: fire `getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)` once on mount, read `recommendations.recs` back off the same hook, and feed that into the **unchanged** `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` mapper (its input is a strict superset of what it read before, so it needed zero edits — confirmed against `use-einstein.js:465-520`'s `fetchRecProductDetails`, not assumed).

**Fix (the concrete diff):**
- `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` — swapped the two interim-hook imports/calls for `useEinstein`/`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS`, added the mount-effect, normalized `recommendations?.recs ?? []` into a local `recs` array, changed `cards`'s source from `products` to `recs`, and changed the render gate from `hasRecentlyViewed ? grid : empty` to a three-way `recs.length > 0 ? grid : (!isLoading && recs.length === 0) ? empty : null`. Docblock rewritten to match (empty-state-gate reasoning, plus a new documented "first-paint window" note — see below). Everything named as "keep unchanged" in the brief (SEO, `<Heading srOnly>`, `APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX` + 112px footer reservation, item-count label) is untouched.
- `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx` — every mock rewritten from the two interim hooks to `mockUseEinstein`, following the exact pattern already committed in `recommended-products/index.test.tsx` (E1). All 11 original test cases kept (same behavioural assertions, same Add-to-Bag ± size-selection coverage), with the old "mid-fetch race" test restructured into the new race-safe-gate test the plan specifically asked for.

No other file touched — confirmed via `git status` before and after (only these two files show modified).

## Pass criteria — evidence

- **`npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.** Ran three times (after the main edit, after the prove-then-restore cycle, and after a final cosmetic comment-wrap fix) — clean every time.
- **`grep -n "useRecentlyViewedHistory\|useRecentlyViewedProductFetch" .../recentlyViewed/index.tsx` returns zero hits.** Confirmed (grep exit code 1 = no match). Note: my first draft of the docblock referenced those two hook names by their exact identifiers in prose, which the grep — a plain substring match — correctly flagged. I rewrote that sentence to describe them without spelling out the identifiers, since the pass criterion is literal, not "no functional reference."
- **Grid renders when `recs.length > 0`; empty state only when `!isLoading && recs.length === 0`; nothing while `isLoading` true with zero recs — proven to fail first.** I temporarily broke the gate (removed the `!isLoading` half, leaving just `recs.length === 0`), ran the new race-safe test, and it failed exactly as expected — the empty-state div (`data-testid="recently-viewed-empty"`, "You haven't viewed anything yet.") rendered during the simulated in-flight window. Restored the real gate, re-ran: passes. Full file re-run afterward: 11/11 green.
- **Add-to-Bag ± size selection resolves the correct variant, assertions kept unchanged.** All three original test cases (no selection → default id/price; a selection → resolved variant; a selection matching nothing → falls back to default) carried over verbatim, only the data-source mock changed. All pass.
- **`npm run test` green, compared against baseline.** Baseline from E1's commit message: 1324/1324. Real result just now: **87 test files passed (87), 1324 tests passed (1324)** — identical count, zero regressions, zero new failures.

**Extra diligence (not in E2's explicit criteria table, but matching what E1's own commit already checked, so the two steps are comparable):** `npm run lint` → 8 errors / 44 warnings, byte-identical to E1's recorded baseline, and none of the reported lines are in either file I touched. `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` → 3 unacknowledged findings, same baseline, same story — none in `recentlyViewed/`.

## Discovered, deliberately not touched

- `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` still appears in this page's own srOnly-heading comment (now line 313). The plan explicitly assigns sweeping this exact stale reference to **E4**, not E2 — left alone on purpose, not an oversight.
- The page's own "badge is always `undefined`" docblock note is stale relative to `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own docblock, which says that gap was closed and confirmed live on 2026-09-09 (the mapper does return a real `badge` today). This inconsistency predates my step, isn't part of E2's named changes, and doesn't affect anything I touched — flagging it rather than quietly fixing a doc issue outside my file list.

## Unverified gaps

- No live/visual check was possible — Einstein is undeployed everywhere reachable, per the plan's own stated ceiling for this whole build. Everything above is code-level proof only.
- My new unit tests mock `useEinstein()` entirely (matching this codebase's own mocking convention and E1's precedent), so they prove the container's branch-selection *contract* given a hook state, not the real hook's state-transition *timing*. That distinction matters for the next item.

## What Marcel is missing

The race-safe gate is implemented exactly as specified, and it correctly closes the "mid-fetch" flash the plan named. But there's a second, related window the plan's text doesn't call out explicitly, and it's worth knowing before this ships: on **every single page load** (not just a shopper's first-ever visit), `useEinstein()` starts every render — including the server-rendered one and the first client paint — at `isLoading: false, recommendations: []` (`use-einstein.js:462-463`). Since `useEffect` only fires after that first paint, there's a real, visible instant where the gate reads "not loading, zero recs" and shows "You haven't viewed anything yet." — then it flips to blank (once the effect sets `isLoading: true`), then finally to the real grid once the Einstein round-trip resolves. The old interim design had the same first-paint property, but its fix-up was a synchronous `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` read (imperceptible); this one is a real network round-trip, so the flash window is no longer instant — it's however long Einstein + the `getProducts` hydration actually take. I documented this precisely in the file rather than silently patching around it, because the gate's exact shape was explicitly called out in the brief as "not yours to redesign" — but whether that's an acceptable interim characteristic or needs a follow-up (e.g. a loading skeleton, or seeding `isLoading` differently) is a call for Marcel, not something I should decide inside this step.
